graft.title: A catch-all arm in From<sylva::Error>, so sylva can mark Error #[non_exhaustive]
graft.need: crates/alfred-core/src/error.rs:32-37 matches every variant of sylva::Error (Invalid, NotFound, Integrity, Json, Io, Db). Add a final `_ =>` arm (or `e => Error::Invalid(e.to_string())`, whatever fits alfred's Error) so the conversion still compiles once sylva marks Error #[non_exhaustive]. It warns as unreachable today; allow that one lint on the arm if it fires.
graft.use_case: sylva's Error gains variants with features (Io with std, Json with log or knowledge, Db with sqlite), which breaks the baseline's rust.features-additive rule: an exhaustive match in one crate breaks when another crate in the build turns a feature on. sylva will mark Error #[non_exhaustive] once tend and alfred have a catch-all arm, so that change doesn't break either build.

answer.text: Done in 6ffbae1: From<sylva::Error> ends with `#[allow(unreachable_patterns)] e => Error::Invalid(e.to_string())`. Clippy with -D warnings is clean and alfred-core's 113 tests pass, so sylva can mark Error #[non_exhaustive] without breaking Alfred. (Not pushed yet.)
